caption_en:
Gaza is the patient. HAMAS is the tumour. 🩺

Every light on the scan is a person. The tumour's roots run under homes, schools and hospitals:
🔹 The White House (14 Nov 2023): HAMAS and Palestinian Islamic Jihad "use some hospitals in the Gaza Strip, including Al-Shifa, and tunnels underneath them ... to hold hostages."
🔹 Feb 2024: the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) showed a HAMAS data centre in a tunnel under the Gaza City HQ of UNRWA, the UN Relief and Works Agency. UNRWA said it did not know.
🔹 July 2014: UNRWA itself reported rockets hidden in three of its vacant schools.
🔹 Gaza: about 41 km long. Tunnels: an estimated 560 to 720 km.

Two options. One bomb: tumour gone, patient gone. Like cutting one artery: the whole body dies. Or surgery: hundreds of small, careful cuts, to remove only the tumour.
🔹 Warnings before strikes: leaflets, calls, texts (some Gazans called them confusing).
🔹 Evacuation corridors and daily pauses in the fighting.
🔹 Pauses so about 560,000 children could get the polio vaccine (World Health Organization, Sept 2024).
🔹 A slow ground operation: 472 Israeli soldiers killed.

And every healthy cell lost is a real person. A real tragedy. That's why the laws of war judge each strike on its own: is the expected civilian harm excessive for the military advantage? Not by comparing death tolls.

The goal was never the patient. Remove the tumour, so the patient can live.

Send this to someone who says "disproportionate".
caption_he:
עזה היא המטופל. חמאס הוא הגידול. 🩺
פצצה אחת: הגידול נעלם, וגם המטופל. כמו לחתוך עורק אחד: כל הגוף מת. או ניתוח: מאות חתכים קטנים וזהירים, כדי להוציא רק את הגידול.
אזהרות לפני תקיפות, מסדרונות פינוי, הפוגות אפילו לחיסוני פוליו. ובתמרון הקרקעי נהרגו 472 חיילי צה"ל.
המטרה מעולם לא הייתה המטופל. מוציאים את הגידול, כדי שהמטופל יוכל לחיות.
